Md Mozaharul Islam, Advocate -----For the Petitioner.
Md Ahasanul Karim, AQM Salimullah and Ruhul Ameen, Advocates ----- For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Doel Apparels Limited ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Judge Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: On an application under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 21 dated 19-10-2010 passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No.2 Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 233 of 2009 allowing the amendment of the judgment and decree dated 13-7-2010 (Annexure-G) to the petition and order No. 9 dated 28-2-2012 passed by the .same Judge in Artha Jari Case No. 61 of 2011 rejecting an application of the petitioner filed under section 28 read with section 57 of the Artha Kin Adalat Ain 2003 (Annexure-M) to the petition shall not be declared illegal and without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Plaintiff-respondent No. 2 GSP Finance Company (Bangladesh Limited) filed Artha Rin Suit for realization of Taka 8,30,51,041 as on 10- 10-2009 from the petitioner and others who took loan for conducting their respective business by an agreement Nos. 1042/L/S/2002 and 1043/L/S/2002 respectively but subsequently in terms of such agreement the petitioner failed to pay the installment and made themselves defaulter. Then the respondent No.2 filed Artha Rin Suit for recovery of the outstanding loan with interest which was decreed in part to the loan of Taka 1,94,00,043 only without taking into consideration of the claim arising out of the loan agreement No. 1043 to the lone of Taka 3,36,50,998. Subsequently on the prayer of the plaintiff under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure such an inadvertent error has been duly rectified by the concerned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat who made the decretal amount of Taka 8,30,51,041 in place of Taka 1,94,00,043 appearing in the operating portion of the judgment and other place wherever it appears. Thereafter, plaintiff decree-holder filed this Execution Case for the decretal amount of Taka 8,30,51,041 in place' of Taka 1,94,00,043 only. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned material change of the operating portion on the judgment and decree the judgment-debtor has invoked this writ jurisdiction alleging that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat preserves no right to change the decretal amount of Taka 1,94,00,043 to 8,30,51,041 with the help of the provision laid down in section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain-2003 read with section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure because it is neither any clerical mistake nor inadvertent omission on the part of the court. Moreover, the observation of the court so far it relates to the decree passed at the first instance still in existence which will not go to support the subsequent increased amount directing the judgment-debtor to pay the same within the period fixed by the court. 

 5. Mr Md Mozaharul Islam, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that since the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has considered both the agreement Nos. 1042 and 1043 at the time of passing the judgment and decree; as such that can be rectified on the ground of arithmetical error or typical mistake. 

 7. On the other hand Mr Ahasanul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2, Financial Institution, has strongly opposed the sale alleging that where court has rectified it's own judgment and decree on the ground of inadvertent error; aggrieved party have no other alternative but to prefer an appeal under section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. In order to circumvent the jurisdiction of the appellate authority there can be no scope to invoke writ jurisdiction because to decide the matter, admitted evidence must be taken into the consideration. With reference to the document exhibit-15 now Annexure-2(A) Mr Karim has pointed out that during the course judgment the learned Judge of the Adalat has absolutely over-looked the two accounts arising out of admitted agreement Nos. 1042 and 1043, sanctioned in favour of the judgment-debtor for which the learned Judge came to an erroneous decision and subsequently he realised it and rectified the bonafide error committed by him under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat read with section 152 of the Code Civil Procedure. 

 10. Referring the above decision the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that judgment-debtor has no other alternative but to prefer an appeal against the impugned judgment and decree for which execution case No. 61 of2011 has been filed but cannot be challenged in writ jurisdiction. 

 12. Be the case as it may the order which has been passed by the court below in rectifying his own judgment and order may be considered as procedural mistake but that cannot be challenged in the writ jurisdiction since there is a statutory forum of appeal where judgment-debtor may prefer an appeal against such impugned judgment and decree.
